$comment: The window onto the desk. Alpaca's official MCP server, pointed at the
competition paper account, so the running system can be interrogated in plain
English: what is open, what did it refuse, what is the account doing.
It is served through agent/mcp_readonly.py, a stdio proxy that ENFORCES
read-only rather than assuming it. Alpaca's ALPACA_TOOLSETS filter does not
remove the order-placing tools - they are built-in overrides, not spec-driven
operations - so a server started with account,trading,assets,news still exposes
place_option_order. The proxy strips every mutating tool out of tools/list and
refuses tools/call for one by name, even if a client never lists first.
Verified: 11 of 35 tools blocked, 24 reads pass through.
Run `python -m agent.mcp_readonly --audit` to see the split.
Execution never goes through here. Every order HALFSPREAD places is an Alpaca
CLI invocation recorded verbatim in data/journal/*.jsonl and replayable by hand,
and agent/execute.py refuses the competition account without an explicit arming
token. The CLI is the agent's hands; MCP is the window.
Keys are read from the environment and are never committed - copy .env.example
to .env and fill it in, or export them in your shell.
